			<font style="display:inline;">The total cost of equipment and furniture and office equipment included in the table above held under capital lease obligations was $0.1 million as of December 31, 2016 and December 26, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation expense, including amortization of property under capital leases, for fiscal years 2016, 2015 and 2014 was $7.0 million, $7.0 million and $6.7 million, respectively.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">8.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Term Debt and Line of Credit</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">ABL Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 18, 2015, the Company entered into a five-year revolving credit agreement with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association (&#x201C;Wells Fargo&#x201D;), as administrative agent, and the other lenders party thereto (with all related loan documents, and as amended from time to time, the &#x201C;ABL Credit Facility&#x201D;), replacing our Prior Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;All commitments under the Prior Credit Facility were terminated and all outstanding borrowings thereunder were repaid effective November 18, 2015.&nbsp;&nbsp;The remaining obligations of the Company and its subsidiaries under the Prior Credit Facility generally are limited to certain remaining contingent indemnification obligations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The ABL Credit Facility provides for a five-year, $50.0 million senior secured revolving credit facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ABL Credit Facility also provides that, under certain conditions, we may increase the aggregate principal amount of loans outstanding thereunder by up to $10.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;On November 18, 2015, we borrowed $21.9 million under the ABL Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;We used the initial borrowing under that facility, together with the proceeds from the Term Loan Credit Facility (described below) to repay all outstanding borrowings under the Prior Credit Facility (consisting of $101.1 million), to pay accrued interest with respect to such loans, and to fund the payment of certain fees and costs relating to the Credit Facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ABL Credit Facility will mature, and the commitments thereunder will terminate, on November 17, 2020. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company and all of its subsidiaries are borrowers under the ABL Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subject to certain exceptions, the obligations under the ABL Credit Facility are secured by a lien on substantially all of the assets of the Company including: (i) a perfected first priority pledge of all the equity interests of the Company, and (ii) a perfected first priority security interest in substantially all other tangible and intangible assets of the Company and its subsidiaries (including, but not limited, to accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, general intangibles, investment property, real property, intellectual property and the proceeds of the foregoing).&nbsp;&nbsp;The obligations under the ABL Credit Facility are also guaranteed by each of the Company&#x2019;s subsidiaries.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Availability of borrowings under the ABL Credit Facility is subject to, among other things, a borrowing base calculation based upon a valuation of our eligible accounts and eligible inventory (including eligible finished goods, raw materials, and by-products inventory), each multiplied by an applicable advance rate or limit, and certain reserves and caps customary for financings of this type.&nbsp;&nbsp;If at any time the aggregate amounts outstanding under the ABL Credit Facility exceed the borrowing base then in effect, a prepayment of an amount sufficient to eliminate such excess is </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">64</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</a></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">required to be made.&nbsp;&nbsp;Availability of borrowings under the ABL Credit Facility is also subject to a bring down of the representations and warranties in such Facility and the absence of any default thereunder (including any such default under our financial and other covenants in our Term Loan Credit Facility described below).&nbsp;&nbsp;Voluntary prepayments of revolving loans under the ABL Credit Facility are permitted at any time, in whole or in part, without premium or penalty.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Borrowings under the ABL Credit Facility bear interest, at the Company&#x2019;s option, at a base rate or LIBOR plus, in each case, an applicable margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;LIBOR is reset at the beginning of each selected interest period based on the LIBOR rate then in effect; provided that, if LIBOR is below zero, then such rate will be equal to zero plus the applicable margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The base rate is a fluctuating interest rate equal to the highest of (i) the federal funds effective rate from time to time plus 0.50%, (ii) LIBOR (after taking account of any applicable floor) applicable for an interest period of one month plus 1.00%, and (iii) the prime lending rate announced from time to time by Wells Fargo.&nbsp;&nbsp;The applicable margin is subject to adjustment based on the Company&#x2019;s Average Excess Availability (as defined in the ABL Credit Facility).&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, to maintain availability of funds under the ABL Credit Facility, we pay a monthly commitment fee of 0.25&#x2013;0.375% per annum, depending on the average ABL Credit Facility balance, on the unused portion of the ABL Credit Facility.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Ongoing extensions of credit under the ABL Credit Facility are subject to customary conditions, including sufficient availability under the borrowing base.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ABL Credit Facility also contains covenants that require the Company to, among other things, periodically furnish financial and other information to the various lenders.&nbsp;&nbsp;The ABL Credit Facility contains customary negative covenant and also requires the Company, together with its subsidiaries, to comply with a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio (as defined in the ABL Credit Facility) upon exceeding certain minimum availability requirements. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Events of default under the ABL Credit Facility include customary events such as a cross-default provision with respect to other material debt. As of December 31, 2016, the Company is in compliance with all covenants of the ABL Credit Facility, except for the requirement to deliver audited financial statements without a going concern opinion.&nbsp;&nbsp;We have obtained a temporary waiver of the going concern qualification until May 15, 2017 from the lenders under the ABL Credit Facility. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We use the ABL Credit Facility, in part, to fund our seasonal working capital needs, which are affected by, among other things, the growing cycles of the fruits and vegetables we process, for capital expenditures and for other general corporate purposes. The vast majority of our fruit and vegetable inventories are produced during the harvesting and packing months of June through September and depleted through the remaining eight months. Accordingly, our need to draw funds under the ABL Credit Facility fluctuates significantly during the year. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2016, there was $32.8 million outstanding under the ABL Credit Facility and the net availability thereunder was $10.3 million. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Term Loan Credit Facility</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Also on November 18, 2015 and concurrent with the execution of the ABL Credit Facility, Inventure Foods and certain of its subsidiaries entered into a five-year term loan credit agreement (the &#x201C;Term Loan Credit Facility&#x201D;), with BSP Agency, LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (&#x201C;BSP&#x201D;), as administrative agent, and the other lenders party thereto.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan Credit Facility provides for a $85.0 million senior secured term loan that matures on November 17, 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan Credit Facility also provides that, under certain conditions, we may increase the aggregate principal amount of term loans outstanding thereunder by up to $25.0 million.&nbsp;&nbsp;As noted above, we used the proceeds of the Term Loan Credit Facility, together with certain proceeds of the ABL Credit Facility, to refinance the indebtedness under the Prior Credit Facility and to fund payment of certain fees and costs related to the Credit Facilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;Unlike amounts repaid under the ABL Credit Facility, any amounts we repay under the Term Loan Credit Facility may not be reborrowed.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan Credit Facility also matures on November 17, 2020. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company and all of its subsidiaries are borrowers under the Term Loan Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subject to certain exceptions, the obligations under the Term Loan Credit Facility are secured by substantially all of the assets of the Company including: (i) a perfected first priority pledge of all the equity interests of the Company, and (ii) a perfected first priority security interest in substantially all other tangible and intangible assets of the Company (including, but not limited, to accounts receivable, inventory, equipment, general intangibles, investment property, real property, intellectual property and the proceeds of the foregoing). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Borrowings under the Term Loan Credit Facility bear interest, at the Company&#x2019;s option, at a base rate or LIBOR plus, in each case, an applicable margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;LIBOR is reset at the beginning of each selected interest period based on the LIBOR rate then in effect; provided that, if LIBOR is below zero, then such rate will be equal to zero plus the applicable margin.&nbsp;&nbsp;The base rate is a fluctuating interest rate equal to the highest of (i) the federal funds effective rate from time to time plus 0.50%, (ii) LIBOR (after taking account of any applicable floor) applicable for an interest period of one month plus 1.00%, and (iii) the prime lending rate announced by Wells Fargo.&nbsp;&nbsp;The applicable margin is subject to adjustment based on the Company&#x2019;s Total Leverage Ratio (as defined in the Term Loan Credit Facility). </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Term Loan Credit Facility requires amortization in the form of quarterly scheduled principal payments of $212,500 per fiscal quarter from March 2016 to September 2020, with the remaining balance due on the maturity date of November 17, 2020.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition to the scheduled quarterly principal payments, the Company is required to make mandatory principal payments out of Excess Cash Flow (as defined in the Term Loan Credit Facility)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Term Loan Credit Facility also contains affirmative and negative covenants that require the Company to, among other things, periodically furnish financial and other information to the various lenders.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Term Loan Credit Facility contains customary negative covenants and also requires the Company, together with its subsidiaries, to comply with a Fixed Charge Coverage Ratio (as defined in the Term Loan Credit Facility) and a Total Leverage Ratio (as defined in the Term Loan Credit Facility).&nbsp; On September 27, 2016, the Company entered into that certain Second Amendment to Credit Agreement with BSP, as the administrative agent, and the other lenders party thereto (the &#x201C;Second Amendment&#x201D;). The Second Amendment defers compliance with the Company&#x2019;s Total Leverage Ratio and Fixed Charge </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

As such, we reclassified all of our outstanding debt as a current liability.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We produce T.G.I. Friday&#x2019;s&#xAE; brand snacks, Tato Skins&#xAE; brand potato crisps and Boulder Canyon&#xAE; Authentic Foods Rice and Bean snacks utilizing a sheeting and frying process that includes technology that we license from a third party.&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the terms of this license agreement, we have a royalty-bearing, exclusive right license to use the technology in the United States, Canada, and Mexico until such time the parties mutually agree to terminate the agreement.&nbsp;&nbsp;Even though the patents for this technology expired in December 2006, in consideration for the use of this technology, we are required to make royalty payments on sales of products manufactured utilizing the technology until such termination date.&nbsp;&nbsp;However, should products substantially similar to Tato Skins&#xAE;, O&#x2019;Boisies&#xAE; and Pizzarias&#xAE; become available for any reason in the marketplace by any manufacturer other than us and such availability results in a sales decline of 10% or more, any royalty obligation for the respective products&nbsp;shall cease.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;">We license the T.G.I. Friday&#x2019;s&#xAE; brand snacks trademark from T.G.I. Friday&#x2019;s under a license agreement with a term expiring in December 2019, subject to automatic renewal for an additional five year term unless we provide notice of nonrenewal on or prior to July 1, 2019.&nbsp; Pursuant to the license agreement, we are required to make royalty payments on sales of T.G.I. Friday&#x2019;s&#xAE; brand snack products and are required to achieve certain minimum sales levels by certain dates during the contract term.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">We license the Jamba&#xAE; brand trademark from Jamba Juice Company under a license agreement with a term expiring in 2035.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the license agreement, we are required to make royalty payments on sales of Jamba&#xAE; products, and are required to achieve certain minimum sales levels by certain dates during the contract term.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">We license the Nathan&#x2019;s Famous&#xAE; brand trademark from Nathan&#x2019;s Famous Corporation under a license agreement with a term expiring in 2031.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the license agreement, we are required to make royalty payments </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

			<font style="display:inline;">We license the Vidalia&#xAE; brand trademark from Vidalia Brands,&nbsp;Inc. under a license agreement with a term expiring January&nbsp;2019.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to the license agreement, we are required to make royalty payments on sales of Vidalia&#xAE; brand products during the contract term.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">10.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Stockholders&#x2019; Equity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our 2015 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;2015 Plan&#x201D;) was approved at our 2015 annual meeting of stockholders.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2015 Plan replaces our Amended and Restated 2005 Equity Incentive Plan (the &#x201C;2005 Plan&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Under the 2015 Plan, we are authorized to issue up to 1,400,560&nbsp;shares of our Common Stock, which number may be increased by up to 250,000 shares subject to any option or award outstanding under the 2005 Plan that are canceled or forfeited for any reason.&nbsp;&nbsp;If any shares of our Common Stock subject to awards granted under the 2015 Plan are canceled, those shares will be available for future awards under such plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2015 Plan expires in May 2025.&nbsp;&nbsp;Awards granted under the 2015 Plan may include: nonqualified stock options, incentive stock options, restricted stock, restricted stock units, performance shares, performance units, and other stock-based awards and cash-based awards. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2016, there were 956,088 shares of Common Stock available for awards under the 2015 Plan.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Restricted Common Stock</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We have issued shares of restricted Common Stock in the form of restricted stock awards and restricted stock units as incentives to certain employees, officers and members of our board of directors (the &#x201C;Board&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted stock awards and restricted stock units granted to members of the Board are granted with a one-year service period.&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted stock awards and restricted stock units granted to the Company&#x2019;s officers vest over three years and typically contain performance restrictions that are required to be achieved over a three year measurement period in order for the shares to be released.&nbsp;&nbsp;The number of performance-based restricted stock ultimately released varies based on whether we achieve certain financial results.&nbsp;&nbsp;Restricted stock units granted to non-officer employees generally vest over three or five years.&nbsp;&nbsp;We record compensation expense each period based on the market price of our Common Stock at the time of grant and, for performance-based restricted stock awards and units, our estimate of the most probable number of shares that will ultimately be released.&nbsp;&nbsp;The related stock-based compensation expense is included in selling, general and administrative expenses.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, the compensation expense is adjusted for our estimate of forfeitures.&nbsp;&nbsp;Recipients of restricted Common Stock are entitled to receive any dividends declared on our Common Stock and have voting rights, regardless of whether such shares have vested.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">During the fiscal years ended December 31, 2016, December 26, 2015 and December 27, 2014, the total stock-based compensation expense from restricted Common Stock recognized in the financial statements was $1.5 million, $1.1 million and $1.1 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no stock-based compensation costs which were capitalized.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our operations consist of two reportable segments: frozen products and snack products.&nbsp; The frozen products segment produces frozen fruits, vegetables, beverages and desserts for sale primarily to grocery stores, club stores and mass merchandisers.&nbsp; The snack products segment produces potato chips, kettle chips, potato crisps, potato skins, pellet snacks, sheeted dough products, popcorn and extruded products for sale primarily to snack food distributors and retailers.&nbsp; Our reportable segments offer different products and services.&nbsp; The majority of our revenues are attributable to external customers in the United States.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also sell to external customers internationally; however, the revenues attributable to such customers are immaterial.&nbsp; All of our assets are located in the United States.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">All products sold under our frozen products segment are considered part of the healthy/natural food category.&nbsp;&nbsp;The products sold under our snack products segment include products considered part of the indulgent specialty snack food category, as well as products considered part of the healthy/natural food category.&nbsp;&nbsp;For fiscal 2016, 2015 and 2014, net revenues of our healthy/natural food category totaled $230.8 million, $238.1 million and $236.6 million, respectively.&nbsp;&nbsp;For fiscal 2016, 2015 and 2014, net revenues of our indulgent specialty snack food category totaled $38.2 million, $44.5 million and $49.1 million, respectively.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">13.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Legal Proceedings</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We are periodically a party to various lawsuits arising in the ordinary course of business.&nbsp; Management believes, based on discussions with legal counsel, that the resolution of any such lawsuits, individually and in the aggregate,&nbsp;will not have a material adverse effect on our financial position or results of operations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Indemnification Request</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On or about February 17, 2016, the Company received a letter from one of its commercial customers requesting indemnity with respect to a lawsuit threatened against the customer in Florida alleging that certain kettle chip products sold by the customer and manufactured by the Company were improperly labeled as &#x201C;natural.&#x201D;&nbsp; On March 7, 2016, the Company informed the commercial customer that the Company had no obligation to indemnify the commercial customer with respect to the matter.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-style:italic;">Litigation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On April 4, 2016, a purported class action captioned Westmoreland County Employee Retirement Fund (&#x201C;Westmoreland&#x201D;) v. Inventure Foods Inc. et al., Case No. CV2016-002718, was filed in the Superior Court in Maricopa County, Arizona. Additional defendants are the Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, and the underwriters of the secondary securities offering that closed September 14, 2014 (the &#x201C;September 2014 Offering&#x201D;).&nbsp; The class action complaint, which was amended a second time on March 27, 2017, alleges violations of Sections 11, 12(a)(2) and 15 of the Securities Act and focuses on the conditions at the Company&#x2019;s former frozen food facility in Jefferson, Georgia.&nbsp; Westmoreland seeks certification as a class action, unspecified compensatory damages, rescission or a rescissory measure of damages, attorneys&#x2019; fees and costs, and other relief deemed appropriate by the court.&nbsp; The Company, its Chief Executive Officer, its Chief Financial Officer and the September 2014 Offering underwriters have not yet responded to the second amended complaint. The Company is vigorously defending against the claims.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">On November 10, 2016, the Center for Environment Health (&#x201C;CEH&#x201D;), represented by Howard Hirsch of Lexington Law Group, filed a lawsuit against Company under the California Safe Drinking Water and Toxic Enforcement Act (known as &#x201C;Proposition 65&#x201D;) (the &#x201C;Act&#x201D;).&nbsp; CEH contends that the Company&#x2019;s potato-based chip products contain amounts of acrylamide in excess of what is permitted under the Act.&nbsp; An Inventure retailer, Bristol </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

Rev. Stat. &#xA7; 407.020, et seq. and 15 C.S.R. 60-8.020, et seq., and unjust enrichment.&nbsp; On February 3, 2017, the Company removed the action to the Eastern District of Missouri. Plaintiff dismissed the removed action without prejudice and refiled a substantially similar complaint in the Southern District of Illinois. The new complaint is brought by Ms. Blair and a new plaintiff, Shannah Burton, and asserts a nationwide putative class.&nbsp; The Company intends to vigorously defend the lawsuit.</font>

Cole, Ashton D. Asensio, Macon Bryce Edmonson, Paul J. Lapadat, Harold S. Edwards, David I. Meyers, and Itzhak Reichman.&nbsp;&nbsp;The lawsuit also names the Company as a nominal defendant.&nbsp;&nbsp;The under seal complaint focuses on the conditions at the Company&#x2019;s former frozen food facility in Jefferson, Georgia and the Company&#x2019;s 2015 and 2016 proxy statements.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plaintiff&nbsp;&nbsp;purports to derivatively assert on behalf of the Company claims for alleged violation of Section 14(a) of the Exchange Act, breach of fiduciary duty, waste of corporate assets and unjust enrichment.&nbsp;&nbsp;According to the complaint, the plaintiff seeks an unspecified award of actual or compensatory damages in favor of the Company; an order directing the Company to take certain actions concerning its corporate governance and internal procedures, including putting forward certain proposals concerning its corporate governance policies and amendments to the Company&#x2019;s Bylaws and Articles of Incorporation for a stockholder vote; an award of extraordinary equitable and/or injunctive relief concerning the defendants&#x2019; trading activities or their assets; restitution from defendants to Inventure consisting of a disgorgement of all profits, benefits and other compensation obtained by defendants; costs and disbursements of the action, including attorneys, accountant and experts&#x2019; fees, costs and expenses; and other and further relief as the court deems just and proper. The Company intends to vigorously defend the lawsuit.</font>

Inventure Foods, Inc., et al.,Case No. 2:17-cv-00910, was filed in the U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona purportedly on behalf of all persons and entities that acquired Inventure securities between March 3, 2016 and March 16, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#x2019;s Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer are also named as defendants.&nbsp;&nbsp;The complaint, which focuses on the conditions of the Company&#x2019;s former frozen food facility in Jefferson, Georgia, asserts claims for alleged violation of Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Exchange Act in connection with the Company&#x2019;s press releases and SEC filings between March 3, 2016 and March 16, 2017.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr. Schoenfeld seeks certification as a class action, unspecified compensatory damages, attorneys&#x2019; fees, costs and expenses incurred in the action, and other relief deemed appropriate by the court.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company intends to vigorously defend the lawsuit.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">16.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Concentrations of Credit Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company maintains amounts on account with financial institutions, which at times may exceed federally insured limits. The Company has not experienced any losses on such accounts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our primary concentration of credit risk is related to certain trade accounts receivable.&nbsp; In the normal course of business, we extend unsecured credit to our customers.&nbsp;&nbsp;We investigate a customer&#x2019;s credit worthiness before extending credit.&nbsp; At December 31, 2016 and December 26, 2015, three customers accounted for 28% of accounts receivable.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">17.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred Compensation Plans</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">We have contributory 401(k)&nbsp;plans covering substantially all of our employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;We may contribute amounts not in excess of the lesser of the maximum deductions allowable for income tax purposes or a specific percentage of our </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">77</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">operating profits, as defined in the plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;We made contributions totaling $0.6 million during each of the fiscal years ended December 31, 2016, December 26, 2015 and December 27, 2014.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">We also sponsor a trusteed, nonqualified savings plan for employees whose contributions to a tax qualified 401(k)&nbsp;plan would be limited by provisions of the Internal Revenue Code.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan allows participants to defer receipt of a portion of their salary and incentive compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;The plan was amended in 2009, and we no longer match any employee contributions to this plan.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants earn a return on their deferred compensation based on investment earnings of participant-selected mutual funds.&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred compensation, including accumulated earnings on the participant-directed investment selections, is distributable in cash at participant-specified dates or upon retirement, death, disability or termination of employment.&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2016 and December 26, 2015, the plan&#x2019;s assets and our liability to participants in the deferred compensation plans was $0.6 million and $0.6 million, respectively, and is recorded in other assets and other liabilities in the Consolidated Balance Sheets.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">On March 23, 2017, the Company sold</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">certain&nbsp;&nbsp;assets, properties and rights of our wholly owned subsidiary, Fresh Frozen Foods, to The Pictsweet Company (&#x201C;Pictsweet&#x201D;) pursuant to an Asset Purchase Agreement, dated as of such date, by and among the Company, Fresh Frozen Foods and Pictsweet (the &#x201C;Purchase Agreement&#x201D;).&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with the Purchase Agreement, Pictsweet acquired Fresh Frozen Food&#x2019;s frozen food processing equipment assets, certain real property and associated plants located in Jefferson, Georgia and Thomasville, Georgia, and other intellectual property and inventory.&nbsp; As consideration for the acquisition, Pictsweet paid the Company $23.7 million in cash.&nbsp;&nbsp;The net proceeds from this transfer were $19.5 million, after payment of professional fees and other transaction expenses, and were used to pay down amounts outstanding under the ABL Credit Facility and the Term Loan Credit Facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;As of December 31, 2016 total assets and total liabilities related to the Fresh Frozen Foods business was $32.2 million and $2 million respectively. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:18pt;text-align:justify;text-justify:inter-ideograph;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">The following unaudited pro forma consolidated results of operations (in thousands, except per share data) assumes the Fresh Frozen Foods sale occurred as of the beginning of the earliest period presented.&nbsp;&nbsp;The unaudited pro forma results include estimates and assumptions regarding decreased interest expense related to debt paid down in connection with the sale and the related tax effects.&nbsp;&nbsp;The pro forma results are not necessarily indicative of the actual results that would have occurred had the acquisition been completed as of the beginning of each of the periods presented, nor are they necessarily indicative of future consolidated results.&nbsp;&nbsp;The pro forma net loss for fiscal 2016 includes $12.6 million related to the valuation allowance recorded against our net deferred tax assets.&nbsp;&nbsp;The deferred tax assets include net operating losses from the Fresh Frozen business that will remain with the Company after the sale. &nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -54pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 9.</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:3pt;">&nbsp;<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:3pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 33pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Changes in and Disagreements with Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.<a name="Item9ChangesinandDisagreements_884853"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">None.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 54pt;text-indent: -54pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Item 9A.</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:3pt;">&nbsp;<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:3pt;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 30pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Controls and Procedures.<a name="Item9AControlsandProcedures_421484"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, have evaluated the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s disclosure controls and procedures (as such term is defined in Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e)&nbsp;and 15d-15(e)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) as of the end of the reporting period covered by this Form&nbsp;10-K.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based upon that evaluation and as a result of the material weakness in internal control over financial reporting as set forth below, the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures were not effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2016 for the purpose of providing reasonable assurance that the information required to be disclosed in the reports we file or submit under the Exchange Act is (i)&nbsp;recorded, processed, summarized and reported within the time periods specified in the SEC&#x2019;s rules&nbsp;and forms, and (ii)&nbsp;accumulated and communicated to the Company&#x2019;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosures.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Management&#x2019;s Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)&nbsp;and 15d-15(f)&nbsp;under the Exchange Act) to provide reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with GAAP.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Management assessed the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2016, utilizing the criteria described in the &#x201C;Internal Control&nbsp;- Integrated Framework (2013)&#x201D; issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Management&#x2019;s assessment included evaluation of elements such as the design and operating effectiveness of key financial reporting controls, process documentation, accounting policies, and our overall control environment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Based on this assessment, management has concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was not effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2016 due to a material weakness in our controls over accounting for trade spend liabilities. We have reviewed the results of management&#x2019;s assessment with the Audit Committee of our Board.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:23.75pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A &#x201C;material weakness&#x201D; is defined as a deficiency or combination of deficiencies in internal control over financial reporting such that there is a reasonable possibility that a material misstatement of the company&#x2019;s annual or interim financial statements will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;line-height:120%;text-indent:24pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">As of December 31, 2016, there was a material weakness in our controls over accounting for and reporting of trade spend liabilities. Specifically, the December 2016 month-end review of the trade advertising accrual at year-end did not identify a trade spend liability estimate that was too low for one key customer account which led to a late year-end adjusting journal entry.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our independent registered public accounting firm, Moss Adams LLP, independently assessed the effectiveness of the Company&#x2019;s internal control over financial reporting, as stated in the firm&#x2019;s attestation report, which is included within Part II, Item 8 of this Form 10-K.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Remediation Efforts to Address Material Weakness </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">To remediate the material weakness described above, we are currently evaluating the controls and procedures we will design and put in place to address this material weakness and plan to implement appropriate measures as part of this effort. Management has developed detailed action plans to ensure the inputs utilized to calculate the trade spend liability are complete and accurate, including an upgrade of the software used to help monitor trade spend liabilities.&nbsp;&nbsp;This new software upgrade is already complete and pulls actual sales data into the sales volume input estimates for open sales promotion plans to improve the accuracy of sales volume estimates.&nbsp;&nbsp;Additionally, a Task Force was created to help </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;">80</font>

		</p>

		</p>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

We cannot assure you that material weaknesses or significant deficiencies will not occur in the future or that we will be able to remediate such weaknesses or deficiencies in a timely manner, which could impair our ability to accurately and timely report our financial position, results of operations or cash flows.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Except as described above, there were no changes to our internal control over financial reporting (as defined in Rules 13a-15(f) and 15d-15(f) under the Exchange Act) that occurred during the three months ended December 31, 2016 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Limitations on Effectiveness of Controls and Procedures</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Company&#x2019;s management, including its Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, does not expect that our disclosure controls and procedures or our internal control over financial reporting will prevent or detect all errors and all fraud. A control system, no matter how well-designed and operated, can provide only reasonable, not absolute, assurance that the control system&#x2019;s objectives will be met. The design of a control system must reflect the fact that there are resource constraints, and the benefits of controls must be considered relative to their costs. Further, because of the inherent limitations in all control systems, no evaluation of controls can provide absolute assurance that misstatements due to error or fraud will not occur or that all control issues and instances of fraud, if any, have been detected. The design of any system of controls is based in part on certain assumptions about the likelihood of future events, and there can be no assurance that any design will succeed in achieving its stated goals under all potential future conditions. Projections of any evaluation of the effectiveness of controls to future periods are subject to risks. Over time, controls may become inadequate because of changes in conditions or deterioration in the degree of compliance with policies or procedures.</font>
		</p>
